statements: In file USD01-12/19/2026-ESTT.I, Sri Ch. Naveen Kumar requested a transfer to Regional Office, Vijayawada on spouse grounds, and this request was received on 15-09-2026.
The proposed transfer would increase the total transfers in the Senior Assistant category to 19, representing 15.8% of the cadre strength and exceeding the ceiling.
The note proposes that the Deputy Secretary may approve the transfer because the Secretary is on leave.
According to Standing Order No.2/2020 of the Department, requests received outside the period of relaxation must be kept pending for consideration during the next general transfers.
quotes: Sri Ch. Naveen Kumar, Senior Assistant, Regional Office, Eluru, has requested transfer to Regional Office, Vijayawada on spouse grounds (Flag A), as his wife is working as Junior Assistant in the School Education Department at Vijayawada. The request was received on 15-09-2026.

18 transfers have already been effected in the Senior Assistant category against a cadre strength of 120, i.e. 15%, and the present proposal would take it to 19 (15.8%); (c) one vacancy exists at Vijayawada.
As the Secretary is on leave, the Deputy Secretary may kindly approve the transfer, and draft orders are put up for approval (DFA).
As per para (e) of Standing Order No.2/2020 of this Department (Flag B), requests received outside the period of relaxation shall be kept pending for consideration during the next general transfers.

statements: The Government noted that some employees with pending vigilance enquiries or disciplinary proceedings were transferred or relieved without the knowledge of the Vigilance wing, which hampered the enquiries.

Consequently, all Departments are instructed that no employee with a pending or contemplated vigilance enquiry or disciplinary proceeding shall be transferred or relieved without prior clearance from the Vigilance section.
Every note proposing an employee's transfer must specifically record their Vigilance clearance status.
In the case of Sri K. Venkata Ramana, his transfer request was not considered in view of a pending enquiry.
Clearance of the Vigilance section is mandatory for transfers.
quotes: It has been brought to the notice of the Government that in some cases employees against whom vigilance enquiries or disciplinary proceedings were pending were transferred or relieved without the knowledge of the Vigilance wing, thereby hampering the enquiries.

All Departments are therefore instructed that no employee against whom a vigilance enquiry or disciplinary proceeding is pending or contemplated shall be transferred or relieved without the prior clearance of the Vigilance section of the Department.
Every note proposing the transfer of an employee shall specifically record the Vigilance clearance status.
Not considered in view of the pending enquiry.
Clearance of the Vigilance section is mandatory, as per the reference 3rd read above.

statements: The Vigilance & Enforcement wing issued a report regarding suspected cartelisation in drain works contracts in three Urban Local Bodies from 2023 to 2025.
The wing conducted a confidential analysis of 46 drain works contracts.
The analysis showed that the lowest bid was within 0.5% of the estimate in 27 cases, which indicates possible bid rotation.

statements: For the 2025 transfers, employees who have completed five years of service at a station as of April 30, 2025, are subject to compulsory transfer.
In computing the station period, periods of leave that do not exceed six months are counted, whereas periods of deputation outside the Department are not counted.
If an employee is transferred within the same headquarters town, the service at both offices is treated as service at one station.
quotes: Employees who have completed five (5) years of service at a station as on 30-04-2025 shall be transferred compulsorily.
Periods of leave not exceeding six months shall be counted towards the station period. Periods of deputation outside the Department shall not be counted.
Where an employee has been transferred within the same headquarters town, the service at both offices shall be treated as service at one station.
